minutes.headline: Select Board approved a Lake Shirley notice of intent 3-1 and renewed most PJ Keating earth removal permits.
minutes.summary: The Select Board, joined by the Sewer Commission for appointments, ratified a new assistant treasurer and building commissioner, then handled a long agenda. It renewed or closed seven earth removal permits, added stop signs, sent the Lake Shirley Improvement Corporation's notice of intent to the Conservation Commission, and accepted a modified Open Meeting Law response. Discussion also covered $10,000 in old primary school repairs, a fall special town meeting date, a package store license petition, and public comment policy.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 3-1, with one abstention, to let the Lake Shirley Improvement Corporation's notice of intent go to the Conservation Commission.
The board renewed PJ Keating earth removal permits 15, 16, 17, 27, 30 and 57, some by split votes with abstentions and with conditions attached.
The board accepted closure of permits 19 and 56 and the Lunenburg Water District permit, and did not renew them.
The board accepted the Open Meeting Law response with the remedial action paragraph replaced by a public comment sentence.
The board approved stop sign locations as submitted, and sent the old primary school repair question to the September 17 workshop.

why_it_matters: Earth removal permit renewals and the Lake Shirley notice of intent decide what excavation and lake work can go ahead, and the Conservation Commission review is where abutters can comment.

Repairs to the old primary school and any independent Lake Shirley water testing would be paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, so the workshop discussion is where those costs would first be weighed.
watch_next: The September 17 workshop, where the old primary school repairs will be taken up with the preservation commission invited.
The special town meeting set for November 12, 2019, with the warrant opening September 10 and closing September 30 at 5:00 p.m.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on most of the core votes (license, permits 15/57/56, appointments), but differ on several counts and on items present in only one record. The key issues are the vote tallies on permits 17/27/30 (3-2 vs 3-1) and Lake Shirley (3-1-1 vs 3-0-1), the unrecorded permit 16 and 19 votes in the official minutes, and the workshop date (Sept 17 vs Sept 10).
